intro: Google Docs for real estate transaction coordinators on Mac is the engine for your daily contract management. Because you work in a browser, your Mac setup matters for speed and accuracy.
tldr: Google Docs runs in your browser, so keep your Chrome or Safari tabs organized.
Use keyboard shortcuts to jump between sections of long contracts.
Create templates for your standard transaction checklists and email templates.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask Lazur where a specific menu item is located.
Keep your file structure in Google Drive clean to find documents instantly.

blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for real estate document management

You do not need a desktop application to run Google Docs on your Mac. You need a fast browser. Chrome is the standard for Google Workspace. It handles the offline mode and extensions better than other browsers.

Install the Google Docs Offline extension from the Chrome Web Store. This allows you to edit contracts when your internet connection drops during a site visit or a remote closing. Go to your Google Drive settings and check the box for offline access. This ensures your latest changes sync the moment you reconnect.
Speed is your primary asset. Using the trackpad for every edit slows you down. Memorize these Mac-specific shortcuts to move through documents faster.

items: ⌘ + Option + M: Add a comment to a contract clause.
⌘ + Shift + V: Paste text without bringing over original formatting.
Option + /: Open the tool finder to search for missing features.
⌘ + Shift + H: Open find and replace to update client names.
⌘ + /: View the full list of keyboard shortcuts.

blocks.text: Creating templates for repetitive closing tasks

You likely handle the same disclosures and checklists for every property. Stop creating these from scratch. Create a master template folder in your Google Drive. Save your standardized contract checklists as templates.

When a new transaction starts, go to File > Make a copy. This keeps your original template pristine while giving you a fresh document for the new address. Use smart chips for dates and people to keep track of closing timelines.
Managing long documents with the outline feature

Real estate contracts can span dozens of pages. Use the document outline on the left side of your screen to jump to specific sections. Apply Heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2) to your document structure so the outline populates automatically.
If you cannot see the outline, go to View > Show outline. This is a lifesaver when you need to verify a specific contingency date in a 50-page purchase agreement.

When you share a draft with an agent or a client, use Suggesting mode instead of Editing mode. Click the pencil icon in the top right corner and select Suggesting. This tracks every change you make. The agent can then accept or reject your edits.
This creates a clear audit trail for compliance. You can see who made a change and when. It prevents accidental deletions of critical contract language.
Handling large files and document limits

Google Docs has a limit of 1.02 million characters per document. This is usually plenty for text, but images and complex tables consume this limit quickly. If your document hits the limit, split it into two files. Name them PropertyName_Part1 and PropertyName_Part2.
For massive PDF files that you need to store, keep them in Google Drive rather than importing them into a Doc. Use a link to the PDF inside your main Google Doc for easy access.

faq.question: Is there a native Google Docs app for macOS?
faq.answer: No. Google Docs is a web-based service. You access it through browsers like Chrome or Safari. You can use third-party wrappers if you want a separate icon in your Dock.

faq.question: How do I work offline in Google Docs?
faq.answer: You must use the Google Chrome browser. Install the Google Docs Offline extension, then enable offline mode in your Google Drive settings.

faq.question: Can I use voice dictation with Google Docs?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use the built-in dictation in macOS or use Lazur to dictate clean text directly into your cursor position.
